verdict.tagline: A grand medieval sandbox buried beneath steep menus and expansions.
for_you_if: you love deep historical sandbox strategy games
you plan to install total conversion mods
you have patience for steep learning curves
not_for_you_if: you expect clear tutorials right away
you are unwilling to buy extensive downloadable content
you experience startup crashes on your system

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players struggle with cluttered menus, unguided tutorials, and steep content pricing.

claims.claim: The tutorial and learning scenario fail to explain core mechanics, leaving new players without guidance on how to declare war or expand territory.

citations.review_text: Pretty unfriendly to new players. Tried the "learning scenario"... it just said it's 1066 do what you feel like and offered no explanation beyond that. I'm all for complicated gameplay, but damn give me a chance to start.

Crusader Kings II is probably a fun game if you already know what you're doing, but it's been a frustrating experience for me as a new player. I've spent 6 hours trying to learn the game and still feel unsuccessful at understanding many of its core mechanics.

The tutorial wasn't very helpful, and the UI is cluttered with information scattered all over the screen, which left me feeling overwhelmed. The game also feels quite outdated by modern standards, both in its interface and how it explains systems to new players.
One of my biggest frustrations was that the tutorial guided me toward building my realm and military strength, but when I tried to expand, I couldn't figure out how to claim Carniaria or declare war to grow my territory. The game didn't do a good job of explaining why I couldn't take those actions or what requirements I was missing.

After 6 hours, I still felt lost and was spending more time searching for explanations than actually playing the game. I can see why longtime fans enjoy it, but for a new player, the learning curve is extremely steep and the game does very little to ease you into its complex mechanics.

citations.review_text: I spent 6 hours on the tutorial. My conclusion is the DLCs are too expensive to bother wasting my time learning how to play the game. UI feels wayy too clunky. The events don't make sense, maybe its just because I don't understand the game... but Sometimes i'm given multiple choice story scenes that feel pointless and interupt the flow of the game... not sure if they're supposed to be funny or make it feel more realistic... I guess if the goal is to make me feel as helpless as I'd feel irl if I suddenly became ruler of a backwards feudal nation (with none of the benefits of actually being there and experiencing it) then i guess the game is a success. I can tell the developers put thought and effort into the game and it looks well crafted... but maybe its overly complex, or I'm just playing it too carefully.... Conquering a signle province seems like a huge ordeal and rebel forces are insanely strong.... also it takes time to rally troops and its hard to sync them so you don't waste time paying troops to stand around. it seems nice, but i don't have the kind of insane time i'd need to throw at this game to enjoy it.

claims.claim: Reviewers complain about the high cost required to purchase the complete collection of downloadable content.

citations.review_text:
[b]Introduction :[/b]
Développé et édité par Paradox Interactive, Crusader Kings II est un jeu de grande stratégie médiévale sorti en février 2012. Ici tu ne diriges pas un pays mais une dynastie : ton but est de faire survivre et prospérer ta lignée à travers quatre siècles d'intrigues, de mariages, de guerres et de complots.

[b]Ce que j'ai aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]👑 une profondeur de simulation dynastique quasiment infinie : mariages arrangés, assassinats, héritages, révoltes de vassaux, chaque partie raconte sa propre histoire et aucune ne se ressemble
[*]🗺️ une rejouabilité colossale, sans objectif imposé : tu choisis toi-même ce que tu veux accomplir sur près de 400 ans, c'est toi qui écris le scénario
[*]⚖️ un équilibre et une richesse politique remarquables, avec une gestion des conflits, des factions et des relations entre personnages vraiment poussée
[*]🇫🇷 une traduction française de qualité et un tutoriel présent qui aide à digérer une prise en main touffue
[/list]

[b]Ce que j'ai moins aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🧩 le fameux effet « jeu à tiroirs » : la montagne de DLC rend presque indispensable d'en acheter pour profiter pleinement de l'expérience complète, la facture grimpe vite
[*]⏳ une courbe d'apprentissage sévère : compte une bonne dizaine d'heures avant que tout fasse clic, les premières parties peuvent être déroutantes
[/list]

[b]Conclusion :[/b]
Crusader Kings II, c'est le magnum opus de Paradox, l'aboutissement de leur quête du wargame parfait. Une fois passé le mur de la prise en main, tu tiens un des jeux de stratégie les plus profonds et addictifs qui soient, une vraie machine à histoires. Faut juste accepter l'exigence de départ et l'appel du portefeuille côté DLC. Si tu aimes les jeux où tu écris ta propre saga, fonce sans hésiter. Recommandé aux amateurs de grande stratégie.

[b]Note :[/b] ★★★★☆

$237.77 to complete my collection for a game made IN 2012! That is FOURTEEN years ago, closer to the date of the very beginning of this franchise in 2004 than today. I have barely played the base game in anticipation of being able to get the whole game one day at a reasonable. Nope... Paradox is central in my change of opinion about gaming as a whole. How can I have any respect for an industry that obviously has none of it for me? "Once we clean up torrents we will be able to offer games at a reasonable price," said the multi-million dollar companies I had sympathy for at that time, like this one. 2012 passed and so did torrents... what happened to the price of this and similar games? THEY GOT MORE EXPENSIVE!!!! Yeah, text book history lesson of factors that led to the Great Depression of monopoly companies with no accountability. 

On a positive note, the base game is now F2P.. the 1st one is always free.

It's free to play because it's a dlc trap. $450 aud for all the dlc on a game from 2012! Wild!!
Putting up a token free to play is just a wolf in sheep skin strat. Dont Little Red Riding Hood your way into their greed snare.

[h1][b] TLDR: A devilishly addicting medieval strategy game bursting with deep mechanics and endless replayability. But its brutal complexity and predatory DLC pricing on an aging title leave a sour aftertaste.[/b] [/h1]

[h1]PROS: [/h1]
➕Steam Workshop integration
➕Deep and involved mechanics
➕Numerous choices to approach situations
➕Addicting “One more turn” type of gameplay


[h1]CONS: [/h1]
➖Overwhelming amount of DLC and an optional subscription….
➖Super high complexity
➖Often vague UI/map elements making things that should be simple, hard

[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative) – [7/10] [/b] [/h1]
The game world takes place on a single map of Earth around Europe, set between the years ~700 and ~1400. The game strives for authenticity, so many of the territories have then original older names. The game goes so far as to even have historical figures that are playable or NPCs, and you can access their Wikipedia page from an in-game link. 
The map itself is 3D, but most of the time appears 2D from a satellite viewpoint. There isn’t much interaction with the map other than clicking on territories to get information. 

There is no predefined narrative, the bulk of the games stories come from events that happen naturally as you play, causing players to create their own stories. It’s the multi-generational hundred years stories of how you and your family built an empire or died trying. 

[h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [8/10] [/b] [/h1]
This game is mechanically vast. It seems like there are multiple solutions to every problem you come across as you play. The majority of your playtime will be spent navigating menus to initiate specific actions. Things like controlling council members, creating plots and laws, wars, managing your court and vassals, it's all very detailed. Most interactions you do have a positive or negative influence on those around you leading to affecting the outcome of future decisions. This is medieval intrigue at its peak. 

The game is…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as requiring a significant time investment to learn.

citations.review_text: took me around 40 hours of playtime to learn this game but its fun

Look, it's not exactly a bad game, it's just alot to understand.  Hours and hours and hours later it is an incredibly frustrating time sink trying to keep a decent lineage when your councils are content with electing the stupidest choice possible and you not being able to stop them because arbitrary game rules stop you from changing election prcoedure without meeting exacting petty rules.  I did enjoy playing it and in a strange way its quite a satisfying game, but it is so infuriating and overly complex that its less of a game and more of a full time job, actually probably more so.  

Not sure why so many medieval 4x and strategy games for the last decade or more have mostly been either too easy (AOE 1 and 2) or trying to recreate actual medieval European politics in what I can only assume is an exact replica of how it went down back then.  Again, it's not exactly a bad thing if thats what floats your goat, and also my mention of AOE isn't a criticism either as it is fun in its own way, just trying to look for a bit of a balance (and no Mount and Blade doesnt count).

While it can be sometimes amusing, and sometimes even helpful, the arbitrary throwing around of events and deaths can also be a bit much, so much so the save scumming often required would put games like the POTC/Sea Dogs games to shame.
Great strategic game, one of my favorite Paradox games. It is hard at the start but when you understand the game is great experience. Huge recommendation!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a character creator and custom kingdoms locked behind paid downloadable content.

citations.review_text:
CKII is the perfect embodiment of the phrase: 'If you live an interesting life and die an interesting death, you won't be remembered as just a footnote in history but an interesting footnote'. If you enjoy roleplaying or Medieval history in general, you will absolutely fall in love with this game. 

The main downside is that the vanilla game, like more than a few Paradox titles, is incredibly bland; playable, of course, but bland. Although the DLC is well worth the expense, in my opinion, I can appreciate that not everyone is willing to fork over exorbitant amounts of money, their soul and their pet cat to greedy Emperor Paradox. At least this game has the benefit of being discontinued.

yeah sure this game in its whole with its DLC is superb, but sorry, there is no way in hell i can reason with a $5 character creator, custom kingdoms being behind a $15 DLC and so many other examples of things that should have never been part of a dlc.
